findings.title: Swift round-trip drops pose and racket ownership
findings.why_it_matters: A desktop-generated portable package loses every player's pose keypoints and each racket's player_id after iOS imports and re-exports it. The iOS importer decodes frames into these narrower Codable structs, stores that decoded representation, and AnalysisStore.export serializes it again, so the loss is permanent and downstream desktop review can no longer render the original pose data or retain racket ownership. Representing both optional fields in the Swift frame types preserves the established v1 frame contract while remaining compatible with iOS-produced records that omit them.

findings.suggested_fix: Reject a package when any required artifact declared by manifest.artifacts is missing, import each required file, and initialize the store status from manifest.status instead of unconditionally setting .complete; only a manifest that is complete should produce a complete imported store.
findings.title: Incomplete imports are silently marked complete
findings.why_it_matters: An analysis folder missing frames, events, or corrections is accepted, and the new store is then marked complete. A damaged transfer can therefore appear successfully imported while silently losing predictions or durable human edits; the Start/Continue action also returns immediately because the store says complete. Requiring the declared artifacts and preserving the manifest status prevents corrupt or paused packages from being converted into false completions.

evidence: contracts/README.md:38 -- Status: running, paused, cancelled, failed, inference_complete, complete.
findings.suggested_fix: Branch on manifest.status during import: retain imported results as complete only when the package is actually complete; for incomplete packages, either rebuild and checkpoint the full tracker/temporal RuntimeState from the imported frames or initialize a fresh zero-frame store and rerun inference from the contained source. Keep the stored status and ResumeIdentity consistent with the chosen path.
findings.title: Imported partial analyses are marked complete
findings.why_it_matters: A paused, cancelled, failed, or otherwise partial v2 package is converted to a completed local analysis during import. The analysis engine then returns immediately for that match, so users cannot continue or regenerate the missing frames; an unanalysed package with empty model provenance can additionally become incompatible as soon as the bundled detector is selected. Preserve the package state and either reconstruct a resumable RuntimeState from imported frames or deliberately restart incomplete imports from frame zero with a matching resume identity.

findings.title: Point-event clip export always rejects
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot export clips for hits or bounces from the desktop event UI: the shared event contract requires point events to have end equal to start, while this handler forwards that zero-length interval to an exporter that requires start to be strictly less than end. Every normal hit/bounce reaches the same deterministic error. Expanding point events to a bounded interval around the timestamp, as the iOS ClipExporter already does, makes the advertised event export usable while preserving rally intervals.

findings.suggested_fix: At end of analysis, checkpoint the final batch with a nonterminal status, export all portable artifacts, then atomically set the store and manifest to complete. Alternatively, when store.status is complete, verify/export the artifacts before returning so a failed export is resumable.
findings.title: Completion is committed before portable export succeeds
findings.why_it_matters: A native analysis can be recorded as complete even when writing frames.jsonl, events.json, corrections.json, or manifest.json fails. On the next attempt, the early complete-status return skips both analysis and export, so the user is left with stale or empty interoperable artifacts and no automatic recovery path. Exporting first and committing complete only after all artifacts succeed keeps the resumable database status aligned with the package users can actually open.

findings.suggested_fix: Make package import asynchronous and run LocalLibrary.importPackage in a detached or dedicated actor task with explicit cancellation checks; await its result before calling the main-actor reload and error-state updates.
findings.title: Package import blocks the main actor
findings.why_it_matters: Importing a large analysis folder can freeze the entire interface while it copies the source video, hashes it, decodes every JSONL frame, and populates SQLite. The import is invoked synchronously from a SwiftUI task, so the progress overlay cannot remain responsive and a multi-gigabyte package can be terminated by the watchdog. Move the synchronous package pipeline to a non-main executor and publish only the final state transition on the main actor.

findings.suggested_fix: When state.nextFrame is nonzero, set AVAssetReader.timeRange to begin at or just before state.lastTimestamp plus manifest.media.origin, allowing AVFoundation to decode the needed keyframe prefix, and keep the time > state.lastTimestamp guard. Verify resumed output against uninterrupted VFR and long-GOP fixtures.
findings.title: Resume decodes every previously completed frame
findings.why_it_matters: Resuming near the end of a long match starts AVAssetReader at the original media origin and decodes the entire completed prefix again, discarding each frame before inference. For the supported two-hour videos, repeated pauses can impose a large and growing restart delay and unnecessary decode energy. Starting the reader near the last committed timestamp while retaining the strict timestamp skip restores only the required GOP prefix and keeps VFR safety.

findings.suggested_fix: Load Corrections once before the decode loop and use the cached value for latestCourt lookups; if live edits during analysis must take effect, refresh the cache only at the existing 60-frame checkpoint boundary or version metadata so it reloads only after a change.
findings.title: Court corrections are decoded for every frame
findings.why_it_matters: Every analyzed frame performs a SQLite metadata query and JSON-decodes the complete corrections object. A two-hour 30 fps match invokes this path about 216,000 times, and the decoded dictionary grows as calibrations and labels are added. Caching corrections outside the frame loop removes this avoidable database and allocation work from the inference hot path.

residual_risks: The simulator smoke test exercises a short valid complete-package round trip, but it does not establish physical-device behavior, long-run thermal/storage recovery, or imported paused-package semantics.

Package manifests authenticate the source video but do not checksum frames, events, or corrections, so post-export corruption of analysis artifacts is detected only when parsing or structural invariants happen to fail.
The app target uses Swift 5 language mode, so strict-concurrency diagnostics do not currently prove all AVFoundation, Core ML, and SwiftUI crossings are Sendable-safe.
Model tensor interpretation and preferred-transform coordinate mapping still require validation with the exact shipped mlpackage and rotated real-device footage.

The simulator smoke harness verifies one short H.264/AAC clip, but audio retention and clip-boundary synchronization remain unverified for the broader source codecs, nonzero timelines, and variable-frame-rate media accepted by the importer.
Covered all five supplied risk divisions through representative paths.
Native smoke bypasses SwiftUI lifecycle and file-picker behavior; VALIDATION.md accurately discloses this.
Termination after the complete SQLite checkpoint but before artifact export leaves stale JSON until explicit export.
Swift Corrections drops desktop corrections.events metadata during import/re-export; immediate events.json state survives, but regeneration portability needs verification.
Native thermal-state pausing remains outside deterministic simulator coverage.

Python stores durable event edit records under an additive corrections.json events key that Swift intentionally ignores. Current events.json import/export preserves the resulting event records, but a future regeneration workflow that relies only on corrections.json could discard those edits unless the durable-edit contract is formalized across both runtimes.

Native analysis has no process-wide or file lock around analysis.sqlite; multiple app scenes could potentially start separate AnalysisEngine actors for the same match, but the reviewed UI does not establish that this is reachable in normal use.
Failure-injection behavior for native disk-full and file-replacement errors was not executed because this review was source-only.
The supplied 180-versus-179 native/ffprobe count difference remains under root investigation and is not classified here as a decoding defect or a passing result.
Native long-match decode speed, peak memory, thermal behavior, and energy use remain unmeasured on a signed physical device.
testing_gaps: No desktop UI/integration test exports a hit or bounce whose contract-valid end equals start.
No iOS import test covers a missing required artifact or a paused/inference-complete manifest.
Shared contract tests do not include semantically invalid cross-platform events such as a hit with a court position.
No test imports packages in each non-complete status and then verifies a correct continue-or-restart path with tracker and temporal-event state preserved.
No UI-level failure injection verifies that event editor content remains presented when SQLite persistence or refresh fails.
No responsiveness or cancellation test covers importing a large package while SwiftUI remains interactive.

The simulator harness exercises the native AVFoundation/Core ML import-analysis-replay-export path locally, but the GitHub workflow only compiles the app and never runs that harness, so these runtime assertions are not a CI regression guard.
Review was static; the malformed-duration package was not imported into a running iOS application.
Read-only source review; no native runtime tests executed.
Simulator fixture does not exercise pause/resume, scene changes or nonzero-frame court corrections.
Desktop create_app job lifecycle lacks behavioral integration coverage for start/poll/cancel/resume, worker-lock release, and terminal status presentation.
Native AnalysisEngine pause/resume is not tested end to end; the smoke harness only runs uninterrupted analysis and manually changes manifest status for package-import rejection.
Python and iOS clip exporters lack failure/cancellation cleanup tests proving partial output removal.
No shared contract fixture exercises a duration above 7200 seconds through both the Python and Swift v2 loaders.
The shared frames fixture has neither player pose keypoints nor racket player_id, so the advertised Python-to-Swift-to-JSON frame round-trip does not exercise the lossy fields.

No cross-runtime test compares Python and Swift verified statistics for a manual, non-excluded event whose reviewed flag is false; Python requires reviewed while Swift currently accepts reviewed OR manual.
No native test injects an AnalysisStore.export failure after the final checkpoint and proves a retry repairs the portable artifacts.
The simulator guard has no fixture whose valid AVFoundation decode count differs from ffprobe, so its oracle mismatch is not covered.
No native lifecycle test opens the same match from two scenes and verifies single-writer behavior.
No long-GOP or near-end resume benchmark demonstrates that restart latency stays bounded for the supported two-hour duration.
No profiling result quantifies per-frame SQLite/JSON correction lookup cost during sustained native inference.
